card.occupation: Not currently working. Last job was an early-morning office cleaner on a contract in Woolwich, which ended about eight months ago. She is on Universal Credit and supposed to be looking for cleaning or kitchen porter work, though she isn't looking very hard.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive in Woolwich at 16 with four GCSEs at low grades and no further qualifications. She started a college catering course at 17 and dropped out in the first term. She did a mandatory food hygiene certificate through a job years ago and has no idea where the paperwork is.
card.household: Lives in a two-bedroom housing association flat on an estate with her son Kyle (16, in Year 11) and her daughter Mia (11, just started secondary). Never married. The kids have different dads. One sends money irregularly and the other doesn't, and she has stopped chasing him. Her mum lives fifteen minutes away in Abbey Wood and helps out with Mia sometimes.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in south-east London. Her family are Woolwich and Plumstead going back a couple of generations, and her grandad worked at the Arsenal before it shut. She has no religion and only ever went to church for weddings and funerals. She sees herself as ordinary London working class and doesn't think about it beyond that.
card.professional_persona: A reliable enough worker once she's actually there, but bad at the admin around a job. She misses texts about shift changes, loses payslips and forgets to sign things. She doesn't get on with supervisors who micromanage and has walked out of one job after a row. She is honest to a fault and will tell you straight if she's broken something or hasn't done it. She prefers early shifts on her own with headphones in, away from people.
card.sports_persona: Doesn't do sport and never has. She walks everywhere because she doesn't drive and the buses annoy her, so she's on her feet a lot and is fit without trying. She will half-watch football if Kyle has it on and nominally supports Charlton because her dad did.
card.arts_persona: Watches the soaps (EastEnders mainly) and reality TV like Married at First Sight or Gogglebox, usually with her phone in her hand. She listens to Magic FM or old garage and R&B from when she was young. She hasn't read a book since school and hasn't been to a museum or a show in years. She isn't against it, it just isn't for her.
card.travel_persona: Hardly travels. A caravan in Kent or Camber Sands a couple of times when the kids were small, and one trip to Benidorm with a mate about twelve years ago. She doesn't have a valid passport. Money is the main reason, but she also isn't bothered. She likes knowing where things are.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks the same handful of things: spag bol, chicken and chips, fish fingers, jacket potatoes, beans on toast. She does a big shop at Lidl when she remembers and the Co-op the rest of the time. Some weeks it's a lot of oven food. She treats herself to a Chinese takeaway on a Friday if money allows and always calls the evening meal dinner.
hobbies_and_interests: scrolling TikTok and local Facebook groups
sitting in the garden at her mum's in summer
online research studies and surveys for a bit of extra money
skills: cleaning quickly and thoroughly when she's in the zone
stretching a small budget, though not with any system
dealing with the council and the school without being fobbed off
being calm and practical in an actual emergency
card.career_goals: No real career plan. She'd like a steady early-morning cleaning or school kitchen job, ideally term-time, so she's home when Mia is. She's vaguely thought about redoing the food hygiene certificate and keeps not doing it. Her main goal is just being less skint.
card.voice: London accent, ordinary south-east London rather than broad. Short answers, a fairly flat delivery and not much small talk. She starts things with 'erm' and uses 'sort of' and 'do you know what I mean' now and then, and sometimes says 'you was' without thinking. She says 'yeah, no' and 'to be fair'. If she doesn't get a question she'll say 'sorry, what was that?' rather than guess. She is comfortable with silence and will just wait for you to carry on rather than fill it. She can be blunt, for example 'no, I don't really do that'. She warms up slightly if you ask about her kids.
card.typing: Mostly lowercase and doesn't bother capitalising 'i'. Few or no apostrophes ('dont', 'im', 'its'). Short answers, sometimes one word, with commas instead of full stops or no punctuation at all. Uses 'n' for 'and' and 'cos'. Occasional typos she doesn't correct. No emojis on a form.
card.with_strangers: Guarded and a bit closed. She's polite enough, but doesn't smile much or ask anything back, and can come across as uninterested or slightly prickly. She doesn't put on a front or exaggerate. If she thinks a question is stupid her tone shows it. She is straightforward and won't pretend to be more than she is, which people tend to find refreshing once they get past the flatness.
small_things: Kyle being on his PlayStation till all hours
the lift in the block being broken
how much the electric's gone up
her mum ringing her five times a day
forgetting a Jobcentre appointment and having to rearrange
deeper_things: worrying about Kyle's GCSEs and him drifting, because she wants him to do better than she did
feeling embarrassed about being on Universal Credit when she's always worked
still being angry with Mia's dad for walking off and never paying anything
knowing she's disorganised and feeling bad about it, but not knowing how to change
being lonely sometimes since most of her old mates moved out to Kent or Essex
her dad dying six years ago and not really talking about it
card.webcam_photo: A slightly low-angled shot from a laptop on a kitchen table, so the ceiling is partly in frame. Daytime, lit flatly by a window off to the left plus an overhead light, which makes her face a bit washed out. A white woman in her mid-forties with a pale complexion and light freckles. Dark blonde hair with grown-out lighter ends, scraped back in a claw clip with loose bits at the front. No glasses. Little or no makeup, slight shadows under her eyes. Neutral, slightly guarded expression, mouth closed, looking just below the camera. She wears a grey zip-up hoodie over a black T-shirt and small gold hoop earrings. Behind her is an open-plan kitchen-living area: a white kitchen cupboard with one door not quite shut, a kettle and a cluttered worktop with a bread bag, a few unopened envelopes and a school letter. Part of a grey fabric sofa with a crumpled throw is visible, along with a radiator with a school polo shirt drying on it and a framed school photo of two children on the wall, slightly crooked.
